title: NAPMP Recipient and Facility Award Stack
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST announced three $100 million materials and substrate awards plus a $1.1 billion Natcast component for the planned Tempe prototyping and advanced-packaging piloting facility.
key_findings: Absolics, Applied Materials, and Arizona State University each received a named $100 million award.
The three projects target glass-core substrates, silicon-core substrates, and wafer or panel-level processing.
The $1.1 billion Natcast component was associated with operating advanced-packaging capabilities at the planned Tempe facility.
why_it_matters: The record disaggregates an advanced-packaging strategy into recipients, technologies, locations, and a facility function that can be checked again.
ftfn_relevance: Defines separate recipient and facility trails instead of one $1.4 billion headline.
Makes later governance, tool, pilot-line, access, qualification, and commercialization evidence necessary.
evidence_limits: The January 2025 record predates Commerce's August 2025 action on Natcast and cannot alone establish the current status of that component.
Awards do not prove operating tools, pilot lines, yields, qualified products, customers, or commercialization.
